outcome: obstetric complications (pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, premature rupture of membranes, uterine atony, placenta previa, oligohydramnios, gestational hypertension, maternal admission to adult ICU)
perinatal complications (gestational age at delivery, birth weight, admission to neonatal intensive care unit)
cohort: The study participants were 120 women who underwent ICSI in an induced cycle using either their own oocytes or freshly donated oocytes, and had male infertility factor and tubal factor.
finding: No significant increase in obstetric and perinatal complications was observed in pregnancies with donated oocytes compared to pregnancies with autologous oocytes among women undergoing ICSI without prior comorbidities.
